title: Ethanol dehydration over ZSM-5 at 573.15 K: upstream rate simplification versus Table-12 adsorption terms
question: Reproduce the upstream ethanol benchmark and quantify inclusion of published product adsorption terms at the same conditions.
written_by: CHEPTA-Lab agent session (Claude); converted from the existing case files, no new execution

warning_notes.note: Stream warnings name PR pairs without k_ij, an ethanol/water k_ij used outside its fitted temperature range, and PR as not the recommended method for the polar liquid (reworded in 0.6.0 to name its MHV1 mixing option; see COMPATIBILITY_0.6.0.md). The top-level qualifications.warnings list does not carry them, so a reader must open the stream warnings. The fixed-T/P rates use yP, so these warnings do not change the component flows but do qualify enthalpies and duties. Identical in the six chepta@0.6.1 runs (see COMPATIBILITY_0.6.1.md).

New on 0.6.2: three listed extrapolations in every run: ideal-gas heat capacity of ethylene (123.15 K above its range 103.99-450 K) and of diethyl ether (25.15 K above 270-548 K), and the ethanol + water PR k_ij set (204.97 K above its range 351.26-368.18 K), each 'an extrapolation, not data'. The two heat-capacity ones are new warnings; the numbers are unchanged from 0.6.1. No estimated pairs (Peng-Robinson with k_ij = 0 for five pairs, as before).

assumptions.statement: Isothermal plug flow, no pressure drop, one vapour phase.
assumptions.basis: Model assumption; broadly consistent with paper Section 3 (SOURCE_LEDGER.md)

assumptions.statement: Rates use partial pressures y P expressed numerically in atm, not fugacities or concentrations.
assumptions.basis: Paper's rate forms; numerical-atm convention kept as printed

assumptions.statement: Peng-Robinson is used as in the upstream example; it does not determine the fixed-T/P kinetic flows.
Total molar flow changes with reaction; this is not the constant-velocity concentration model of paper Section 4.4, so Figure 8 is not reproduced.

unresolved_inputs.item: Pressure-unit convention of Keq1 and Keq2 (Table 8 header atm^-1 versus different pressure powers in Equations 4 and 14) and the printed k1 unit
unresolved_inputs.consequence: Numbers are used as printed with a numerical-atm convention; no thermodynamic standard state is established.
unresolved_inputs.next_action: A person resolves the convention from the paper or its underlying source before any kinetics target is accepted.

unresolved_inputs.item: Original experimental partial pressures, rates and their uncertainty
unresolved_inputs.consequence: Agreement between two numerical solvers is not agreement with experiment.
Transfer to another ZSM-5 is not supported.
unresolved_inputs.next_action: Obtain from the original experimental source.

unresolved_inputs.item: Bounds on the fitted kinetic parameters
unresolved_inputs.consequence: No sensitivity range can be stated; none is invented.

limitations: Numerical benchmark of two rate-model variants of one reactor; not two process routes and not a route recommendation.
No experimental validation; Figure 8 of the paper is not reproduced.
Six runs on CHEPTA commit c1adf6b (between releases) the same six requests on chepta@0.6.0 and again on chepta@0.6.1 (identical numbers); engine agreement is not experimental validation.
Human engineering, source and rights reviews are pending.

chepta@0.6.2 (2026-11-13): the six runs give the same numbers as 0.6.0 and 0.6.1; 0.6.2 lists three extrapolations (two ideal-gas heat capacities, one k_ij set) that earlier versions used silently or only partly warned about; whether strict mode would refuse them is untested.
